doc.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

title: Deciding on music and dropping out of Utica College
summary: A counselor said guitar could not be a major, so he studied English at Utica College until a road offer came.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And was there a point in your life that you said hey, this could be my career?

You know I think I’ve always felt that, even though, in high school when I thought I wanted to go into music, I talked to my counselor who said “well you can’t major in guitar, there is no school that does that.” Of course this was wrong because I graduated in 1964. Berklee was already in existence. There were places in the southern part of the United States that had guitar majors. This man was just unaware of that. This was pre- Internet, pre-communications. He didn’t know. So he said “well you can either major in another instrument or do something else.” So I went to my next strongest subject which was communication, and I majored in English at Utica College. And then halfway through my sophomore year I got an offer to go on the road with a musician and — no contest. I just dropped out.
